- When sentiment is consistently high (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior peak), model often overshoots and fails to correct; apply downward bias of 2–5% for 3–7 days post-spike.
- If sentiment is low (≤0.33) and price is trending down, model often underestimates further decline; add 1–3% downward bias for next 7–14 days.
- Model frequently overcorrects after mean reversion; if price drops sharply then rebounds, forecast should lag the true rebound by 1–3 days.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overestimate early in the forecast window (first 5–7 days); apply 1–2% downward adjustment to first 5 days.
- When sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67), model often averages out; use sentiment-weighted smoothing: higher sentiment → higher forecast, lower → lower, but cap at ±2% deviation from recent 5-day average.
